evidence: "Group by time slot"; "backtracking over time slots, using bitmasks for specialists and machines"
affordance_in_statement: The roster must utilize every specialist, every machine, and every time slot exactly once across the chosen configurations.
removal_suggestion: No wording-only removal is viable: the one-per-time-slot and distinct-specialist/machine constraints are the intrinsic exact-cover problem. Defeating this approach would require changing the computational task or immutable bounds.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Processes time slots one at a time and searches for distinct specialist/machine pairs using bitmasks.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The roster must utilize every specialist, every machine, and every time slot exactly once across the chosen configurations.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its DLX/exact-cover implementation is incorrect or mishandles the search/output despite the exact-cover formulation being conceptually appropriate.
Uses naive backtracking for a three-way matching problem, causing exponential search and TLE on adversarial instances.
Reduces the problem to ordinary bipartite matching/Hungarian matching, which does not enforce simultaneous uniqueness of the third coordinate.

recommended_edit: No permitted single edit can reliably defeat the surviving approach: its affordance is the core structure of the required roster rather than incidental wording.
regression_risk: Rephrasing the constraints or adding explicit exact-cover terminology could make the already-defeated implementations easier to repair.
